content:
Formula: RSA Asymmetric Cryptosystem
Exact Expression: c \equiv m^e \pmod n \quad \text{and} \quad m \equiv c^d \pmod n
Definitions: Public-key asymmetric cryptosystem based on the computational intractability of the prime factorization problem for large semiprime integers.
Derivation/Reference: Ron Rivest, Adi Shamir, & Leonard Adleman, A Method for Obtaining Digital Signatures and Public-Key Cryptosystems (Communications of the ACM, 1978); Clifford Cocks (GCHQ, 1973)
Example: p=61, q=53 -> n=3233, phi=3120. Choose e=17 -> d=2753. Message m=65 -> c = 65^17 mod 3233 = 2790; Decrypt: 2790^2753 mod 3233 = 65
Domain: cryptography
Assumptions: p and q are secret large random primes; gcd(m, n) = 1 (or protected via PKCS#1 OAEP padding)
Common Errors: Using textbook RSA without randomized OAEP padding (leaves cipher vulnerable to Coppersmith and chosen-ciphertext attacks)
